title: How do we make the zoom lines for nine point eight seven six?
description: Zoom lines are made digit by digit for 9.876 and for 0.407, which has a zero digit in the middle. Keeko doubts the second zoom for 0.407 and picks the digit seven instead of the first digit after the point.
teaching_notes: One idea: follow the digits in order, and a zero digit also gives a zoom, the very first gap. Watch for students who skip the zero or jump to the last digit.

source: Make the zoom lines for (a) 9.876 and (b) 0.407.
video_script.why: The child has zoomed in to locate a decimal and now builds the zoom lines for two new decimals.
video_script.substitution: Write the digits in order, and zoom into one gap for each digit, marking the last part.
video_script.anchor: two blank zoom lines of the book, one for 9.876 and one for 0.407
video_script.wrong_answer: zero point seven to zero point eight
video_script.wrong_move: Uses the digit 7 for the second zoom of 0.407 instead of the first digit after the point.
video_script.payoff_line: A zero digit gives the first gap of its zoom

final_answer.spoken: for nine point eight seven six zoom nine to ten, nine point eight to nine point nine, nine point eight seven to nine point eight eight, and mark the sixth part; for zero point four zero seven zoom zero to one, zero point four to zero point five, zero point four zero to zero point four one, and mark the seventh part

maths_rules: zoom 9 to 10, then 9.8 to 9.9, then 9.87 to 9.88, mark the 6th of 10 parts
zoom 0 to 1, then 0.4 to 0.5, then 0.40 to 0.41, mark the 7th of 10 parts
the hundredths digit 0 gives the first gap 0.40 to 0.41
video_script.design: Two blank zoom lines stay on screen. Each digit draws one new line below the last, in the same colour for the chosen gap.

beats.on_screen: title card From your book; two empty stacks of zoom lines labelled 9.876 and 0.407

marks.ask: the two decimals appear above the empty stacks

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about zoom lines.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>We must make zoom lines for nine point eight seven six.
We must also make them for zero point four zero seven.

beats.on_screen: the two empty stacks of zoom lines stay on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits beside the empty lines

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: each digit after the point = one more zoom; a zero is also a digit

marks.each: each digit lights up with its own zoom
marks.zero: a zero digit lights up too

narration: <bookmark mark='each'/>Each digit gives one zoom, and the digits come in order.
<bookmark mark='zero'/>A zero is also a digit, so it also gives a zoom.
<bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the decimals nine point eight seven six, and zero point four zero seven.

beats.on_screen: To find: the zoom lines for each decimal
narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to draw each zoom line, and mark the decimal on the last one.

beats.on_screen: 9.876: units digit 9, zoom 9 to 10; tenths digit 8, zoom 9.8 to 9.9

marks.u: the units digit lights up and the first line is drawn
marks.t: the tenths digit lights up and the second line is drawn

narration: <bookmark mark='u'/>Step one, for nine point eight seven six, the units digit is nine. The first zoom runs from nine to ten.
<bookmark mark='t'/>The tenths digit is eight. The second zoom runs from nine point eight to nine point nine.

beats.on_screen: hundredths digit 7, zoom 9.87 to 9.88; thousandths digit 6, mark the 6th of 10 parts

marks.h: the hundredths digit lights up and the third line is drawn
marks.th: the sixth part is counted and marked

narration: <bookmark mark='h'/>Step two, the hundredths digit is seven. The third zoom runs from nine point eight seven to nine point eight eight.
<bookmark mark='th'/>The thousandths digit is six, so mark the sixth of ten parts.

beats.on_screen: 0.407: units digit 0, zoom 0 to 1; tenths digit 4, zoom 0.4 to 0.5

marks.u: the units digit lights up and the first line is drawn
marks.t: the tenths digit lights up and the second line is drawn

narration: <bookmark mark='u'/>Step three, for zero point four zero seven, the units digit is zero. The first zoom runs from zero to one.
<bookmark mark='t'/>The tenths digit is four. The second zoom runs from zero point four to zero point five.

beats.on_screen: hundredths digit 0, first gap 0.40 to 0.41; thousandths digit 7, mark the 7th of 10 parts

marks.h: the zero digit lights up and the first gap is chosen
marks.th: the seventh part is counted and marked

narration: <bookmark mark='h'/>Step four, the hundredths digit is zero. A zero takes the very first gap, from zero point four zero to zero point four one.
<bookmark mark='th'/>The thousandths digit is seven, so mark the seventh of ten parts.

marks.a: the first stack of lines is shown in full
marks.b: the second stack of lines is shown in full

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>A zero digit gives the first gap of its zoom.
<bookmark mark='a'/>Nine point eight seven six needs four lines, ending with the sixth part marked.
<bookmark mark='b'/>Zero point four zero seven needs four lines too, ending with the seventh part marked.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the zoom lines
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: a speech bubble: second zoom of 0.407 is 0.7 to 0.8; the first digit after the point is 4; the bubble is crossed out

marks.fix: the digit four lights up first
marks.order: the digits are numbered in order

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the second zoom is zero point seven to zero point eight.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But the first digit after the point is four, not seven.
<bookmark mark='order'/>We follow the digits in order, and a zero is also a digit.
